source.title: Uncovering Magnetic Phases with Synthetic Data and Physics-Informed Training
source.authors: A. Medina; M. Arlego; C. Lamas

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendix and references.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports neural-network generalization to Monte Carlo spin configurations, but the task is phase classification in a physical system using synthetic training configurations. It does not test memorization of arbitrary labels, natural-label generalization, or the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, size, sharpness, or memorized-example claims.
record.gate_note: The reported generalization results concern configurations outside the synthetic training regime, including finite-temperature and diluted Ising configurations. These are out-of-distribution results, which the claim explicitly separates. The study does not report train-versus-test error on natural labels or arbitrary-label memorization.
record.test_reason: The study measures magnetic-phase classification, transition estimates, and reconstruction error after synthetic-data training. None tests V1–V8: the width sweep lacks training-error or interpolation-threshold measurements, and dense classifiers and convolutional autoencoders perform different tasks rather than a controlled architecture comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that synthetic-trained dense networks and convolutional autoencoders can identify magnetic phases and estimate transition boundaries beyond their training regime. They interpret reconstruction asymmetry as a ReLU-related architectural bias that enhances sensitivity to symmetry breaking.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses synthetic physical configurations and evaluates phase classification and reconstruction on Montecarlo spin configurations; it does not use the claim's arbitrary-label memorization or natural-label generalization recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Hidden-layer size affects phase classification and transition estimates. ReLU-induced magnetization asymmetry affects reconstruction error. Near the percolation threshold, the maximum-variance criterion becomes unreliable; the low-temperature MSE-splitting criterion gives different accuracy at ρ ≥ 0.6 and ρ = 0.55.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic-trained dense networks classify Monte Carlo configurations at unseen temperatures and dilution levels; the fitted critical density is 0.597(5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training on ideal synthetic spin configurations can support magnetic-phase identification outside the training regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Ferromagnetic identification improves markedly at five or more hidden neurons, while transition-temperature estimates stabilize only above 400 neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hidden-layer width affects phase identification and the stability of inferred critical temperatures in synthetic-trained dense networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Reconstruction error signals phase structure and magnetization sectors; transition detection through maximum variance becomes unreliable near percolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Synthetic-trained convolutional autoencoders can detect magnetic-phase structure, with sensitivity depending on dilution and magnetization sector.

fits_no_version.finding: Including random spin configurations in training leaves down-magnetized configurations with higher reconstruction error than up-magnetized and disordered configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reconstruction asymmetry can persist after disordered inputs are included in training; the authors attribute it to architectural bias.

record.code_released: not stated; implementation and training data available upon request
record.peer_reviewed: Computational Materials Science (venue as stated; submitted to Elsevier)
record.problems: The study does not report train/test error or standard classification accuracy for the claim's settings. Several outcomes are presented graphically without numeric values in the text. The authors state that the maximum-variance criterion becomes unreliable near the percolation threshold. No control comparison for the claim's versions is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Results about the listed claim versions are not reported.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe; chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Held-out error as width increases beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce those effects.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to none. Their cannot_determine states concern V1–V8, not whether the reported physics findings occurred. Distribution shift alone is not an exclusion rule; the decisive issue is that the experiments do not measure the comparisons or effects named by these versions.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out accuracy comparison on natural labels; the tasks are physical phase classification.
No width sweep past the zero-training-error interpolation threshold or test-error measurement; hidden-neuron results concern phase classification and transition estimates.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison on image classification; the convolutional autoencoder is used for spin-configuration reconstruction.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch generalization-gap measurement.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap measurement.
No memorized-example removal or retraining experiment.

rows.subject: DNN
rows.size_stated: 1600 input neurons; single hidden layer, size varied; 2 output neurons for diluted-model transition estimates
rows.stage_stated: trained on synthetic ideal configurations; used to classify Montecarlo configurations
rows.operation_detail: Classified Montecarlo spin configurations across temperature and dilution, then estimated phase probabilities and transition temperatures.

conditions.value: ideal configurations from fully occupied lattice; no finite-temperature or vacancy information

rows.measure: Phase probabilities and transition-temperature estimates; test error not reported.
rows.value: The DNN classified Montecarlo configurations across temperature and dilution values absent from training; fitted critical density ρc = 0.597(5).
rows.note: This is phase classification under distribution shift, not natural-label test error or arbitrary-label memorization.
rows.check: The reported phase-boundary fit is supported by Section 2.3, but it measures none of V1–V8.

rows.subject: DNN
rows.size_stated: Single hidden layer; 1 to 1000 neurons considered
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden-layer neuron count and evaluated phase probabilities and transition-temperature estimates.
rows.measure: Ferromagnetic phase probability and predicted critical temperature; test error not reported.
rows.value: For n ≥ 5, the model rapidly reaches near-perfect classification of the ferromagnetic phase; the predicted Tc stabilizes only when the hidden layer exceeds 400 neurons.
rows.note: The reported outcomes are classification and transition-estimation behavior, not train/test error.
rows.check: Width affects phase probabilities and transition estimates, but zero training error and held-out error beyond interpolation are not measured. Near-perfect ferromagnetic identification is not an overall classification-accuracy estimate.

rows.subject: Convolutional autoencoder (CAE)
rows.size_stated: 8 filters in first and final convolutional layers; nCAE = 8 intermediate filters
rows.stage_stated: trained for 150 epochs on ideal ordered synthetic configurations
rows.operation_detail: Measured reconstruction MSE on Montecarlo configurations across temperature for the pure Ising model.

conditions.value: ideal ordered configurations; no Montecarlo samples or disordered configurations

rows.measure: Mean squared reconstruction error (MSE) versus temperature.
rows.value: Average MSE increases with temperature and eventually stabilizes at a high value in the disordered regime.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation shown as shaded region; numerical values not stated.
rows.note: The measure is reconstruction error under distribution shift, not classification test error.
rows.check: Temperature-dependent reconstruction MSE measures none of V1–V8; its increase is not a generalization gap.

rows.subject: Convolutional autoencoder (CAE)
rows.size_stated: 8 filters in first and final convolutional layers; nCAE = 8 intermediate filters
rows.stage_stated: trained for 150 epochs on ideal ordered synthetic configurations
rows.operation_detail: Compared reconstruction MSE for configurations grouped by the sign of total magnetization.
rows.measure: Mean reconstruction MSE by magnetization sector.
rows.value: Negative-magnetization configurations have much higher MSE; their MSE can exceed that of disordered high-temperature configurations.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations shown in Fig. 8; numerical values not stated.
rows.note: This result reflects reconstruction behavior associated with the model and training setup, not the listed generalization-gap measure.
rows.check: Magnetization-dependent reconstruction error measures architectural asymmetry, not any listed version.

rows.subject: Convolutional autoencoder (CAE)
rows.size_stated: 8 filters in first and final convolutional layers; nCAE = 8 intermediate filters
rows.stage_stated: trained on fully occupied ideal configurations, without vacancies or thermal fluctuations
rows.operation_detail: Measured reconstruction error and its variance on diluted-model Montecarlo configurations across temperature and density.
rows.measure: Average MSE and standard deviation versus temperature; transition-temperature estimation from maximum variance.
rows.value: As ρ decreases, the temperature where MSE grows abruptly shifts lower; near the percolation threshold, the variance peak becomes less pronounced and the maximum-variance criterion becomes unreliable.
rows.uncertainty: 300 Montecarlo-generated patterns per reported point; numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The paper reports a limitation in this OOD phase-detection method near the percolation threshold.
rows.check: The limitation concerns phase-transition detection near percolation, not a partial effect under any listed version.

rows.subject: Convolutional autoencoder (CAE)
rows.size_stated: 8 filters in first and final convolutional layers; nCAE = 8 intermediate filters
rows.stage_stated: trained on fully occupied ideal configurations, without vacancies or thermal fluctuations
rows.operation_detail: Clustered low-temperature MSE curves and compared cluster assignments with the sign of total magnetization.
rows.note: The study uses the MSE split to infer magnetic order and a percolation threshold.
rows.check: The accuracy is for K-means clustering of reconstruction errors against magnetization sign, not a direct classifier accuracy or a measure of any listed version.

rows.subject: Convolutional autoencoder (CAE)
rows.size_stated: 8 filters in first and final convolutional layers; nCAE = 8 intermediate filters
rows.stage_stated: trained on fully occupied ideal configurations, without vacancies or thermal fluctuations
rows.operation_detail: Clustered low-temperature MSE curves and compared cluster assignments with the sign of total magnetization.
rows.note: This is below the paper's stated 5% misclassification threshold.
rows.check: Approximately 90% clustering accuracy implies approximately 10% misclassification, which exceeds the 5% threshold; the record's note incorrectly says it is below that threshold. This measures no listed version.

rows.subject: Convolutional autoencoder (CAE)
rows.size_stated: 8 filters in first and final convolutional layers; nCAE = 8 intermediate filters
rows.stage_stated: trained on synthetic configurations including random patterns
rows.operation_detail: Measured reconstruction MSE on pure Ising Montecarlo configurations after adding random spin patterns to the synthetic training set.

conditions.value: ordered and fully disordered random configurations

rows.value: At low temperatures, error is minimal for up configurations and significantly larger for down configurations, despite down configurations being structurally simpler than high-temperature disordered states.
rows.note: This relaxed setup is described as no longer qualifying as pure anomaly detection.
rows.check: Random spin inputs are not random labels. Reconstruction asymmetry after including these inputs does not test memorization capacity or another listed version.
